sections.body: Forestry includes forest maintenance and timber production, and daily tasks vary by site and plan. The crew must know the work location, exit routes, how to contact the leader, and where to assemble in an emergency. Weather, terrain, and distance from roads can change conditions; workers must not change routes or tasks on their own.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before departure, listen to the instructions, repeat the location and task, check communication equipment, and confirm the contact person. Tell the crew if a radio battery is low or a route is impassable. If the weather worsens or the plan is unclear, stop preparations and ask for confirmation.

Practice scenario: A worker receives a map with a new work point, but the radio cannot connect to the leader.
Suggested response: Do not enter the site. Check the equipment as instructed and report the communication problem so a contact route can be confirmed.

sections.body: Forest terrain may include slippery slopes, roots, holes, loose rocks, dead trees, and hanging branches. Watch the areas above and below, keep your distance, and use approved routes. Rain, wind, fog, or darkness can change the risks; reassess conditions with the leader.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Walk at a pace that lets you see where you are stepping. Do not pass beneath a tree or branch that appears unstable; mark hazards as the crew requires. If the ground shifts or visibility drops, notify the team and wait for instructions. Do not try to move a tree or heavy rock alone.

Practice scenario: After rain, the path to the work site has subsided ground, and a large branch hangs over the route.

sections.body: Forestry work involves hazards from falling objects, sharp tools, machinery, noise, weather, and terrain. Select equipment such as a helmet, eye or face protection, hearing protection, gloves, work boots, and protective clothing according to the task and company rules. Chainsaw work requires suitable training and assignment.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Before work, check equipment for damage, fit, fasteners, and suitability. If a helmet is cracked, a strap is damaged, or protection is unsuitable, do not start; request a replacement. Do not borrow or operate equipment you have not been trained to use, even if a coworker asks for quick help.

Suggested response: Set the bundle aside, do not plant it, and ask the leader to verify the species before work resumes.

sections.body: Vehicles and timber-moving equipment have blind spots, shifting loads, and turning areas. Never stand beneath a load or in a vehicle route. Only authorized operators may control the equipment. Before movement or loading begins, everyone must understand the signals, route boundaries, and waiting zones.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Stay in the designated waiting area, maintain visual contact with the signaler, and do not cross behind moving equipment. If a load shifts, a warning sounds, or someone enters the route, give the stop signal according to procedure and move to a safe place. Report damage or road conditions.

Practice scenario: A log shifts on a heavy-equipment load while a worker stands beside the route to signal.
Suggested response: Give the stop signal as required and move to the safe zone; tell the operator and leader that the log has shifted.

sections.body: Forest soil stores water and supports growth. Equipment routes and unsuitable work can erode the surface or carry sediment into waterways. Marked plots and routes help limit disturbance. If a worker finds standing water, erosion, or a material leak, report it and do not move the material yourself.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Use the designated routes and storage areas. Do not wash tools or dump liquids into waterways. If you see mud entering a ditch or cracked soil, stop movement at that point and notify the leader. Follow directions to secure the area without blocking a channel or damaging vegetation.

Practice scenario: After rain, a vehicle wheel leaves a deep rut leading toward a water channel.
Suggested response: Stop the vehicle in a safe place, report the rut and direction of flow, then wait for the leader to decide on the next route.

sections.body: Field workers may find damaged trees, pest activity, smoke, fire, rubbish, or leaking containers. First, keep your distance, warn the crew, and report the location and visible signs. Pest control, firefighting, and hazardous-material handling must be carried out by designated people under the applicable plan.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Record the plot, time, direction, and observable signs; do not state a cause that has not been established. If there is smoke or fire, alert the crew through the emergency channel and follow the evacuation route. Do not touch a leaking container or transport waste by vehicle without instructions.

Practice scenario: A worker sees light smoke and smells something burning in an area that has not been inspected.
Suggested response: Stay away, alert the crew and leader through the emergency channel, and follow the designated evacuation route.

sections.body: At the end of the job, confirm that all people and tools are accounted for, review the plot, and record results using company units. Reports must distinguish completed quantities, damage, materials on hold, and unfinished tasks. Closeout ensures field issues are not overlooked when the crew leaves.
sections.title: Work Concepts and Standards

sections.body:
Inspect your assigned area, return tools according to the checklist, and compare output quantities with the records. Report locations and the status of markers, routes, or hazards requiring follow-up. Do not declare an area safe if it has not been inspected, or alter quantities to meet a target.

Practice scenario: At the end of the day, one communication device is missing, and a muddy route needs another check.
Suggested response: Tell the leader before leaving the plot, look for the device according to procedure, and record that the route has not been declared safe.
